narrative.northStar: The Rhodonite Specimen, put to work
narrative.overview:
The tools are cut from the same stone as itrium.id. That site is The Rhodonite Specimen (`DESIGN.md` in the `website` repository): a graphite matrix with a pink vein, where gray is the body and pink marks what a visitor should find. Here the specimen leaves the display case and goes onto the workbench. The world is the same: Plus Jakarta Sans for everything, graphite and paper, pastel pink with its two deepenings, flat tonal surfaces, pills and soft corners, one drawn arrow. Only the job changes. itrium.id persuades; a tool gets out of the way. The index is one narrow strip of line items down a quiet ground: each tool, each promise and the point itself as a row, the name on the left and its value set right in tabular figures, groups split by dashed rules, and one heavy closing row over the one pink pill. It reads like the slip a table is used to, without dressing as one: no torn edges, no prices, no shop header. On a tool page the stone keeps its earlier form for now, a slim title band with the work directly under it, because the person using it is at a restaurant table with a phone in one hand and a group waiting. The strip was proven on the index first; the tool pages are to follow it.

Components are soft and sure-footed, and tactile without being playful. Every control has a round, generous target that a thumb finds the first time (2.75rem on touch screens) and an edge you can see (3:1 against the page and the card). They feel good to press but never perform. Density is calm but working: forms sit in a narrow column of 36 to 42rem, inset lists and notes nest one tonal step down inside cards, and the running total stays at the bottom of a phone's screen while the bill is made.

Light and dark are equal. Each follows the visitor's system, and neither is a courtesy version of the other: every new pairing is designed and checked in both. The system refuses what itrium.id refuses: generic SaaS ornament (gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers), drop shadows on anything but a floating list, pure black and white, decorative pink, and small labels above headings. It also refuses what only a tool can get wrong: a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen, and state shown by color alone.
keyCharacteristics: One stone with itrium.id: the same tokens, typeface, radii, button shapes and arrow.

The index is one strip of rows, name left and value right in tabular figures, ending in a heavy closing row and the one pink pill. A tool page opens with a slim title band, then the tool. Strip, ground and band follow the theme: a step off the page, never the other theme's color.
Light and dark are equal. Both follow the system, unless System, Light or Dark is chosen in the footer.
Flat surfaces with tonal steps. The only shadow is under the open searchable list.
Every control has a 3:1 edge (`--control-border`), a target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens, and 16px text on touch screens so iOS doesn't zoom.
Pink marks the primary action, focus, what's selected, and the way onward, and nothing else.
Motion is CSS only and off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks something: the primary action, focus, what's selected, or the way onward. If you can't say what a pink element marks, it should be gray. In a tool, one pink button per view; on the index, one pink pill at the strip's end, with the rows' arrows in rose text as their way onward and nothing else pink.

rules.name: The Two Borders Rule
rules.body: `--border` is for lines nothing depends on, such as card edges and dividers. Anything a person has to find in order to use it gets `--control-border`.

rules.name: The Graphite Text Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite, never white. On light backgrounds pink text is rose text and pink lines are deep rose. Pastel pink is never text or a line there.

rules.name: The Every-Surface Rule
rules.body: Contrast is checked on every surface text sits on: page, card, inset list, note, running total, the index's strip and its ground, in both themes. Text needs 4.5:1. Focus outlines, control edges and state lines need 3:1.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans does everything. Never add a second family, and never load a font from another domain.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A heading is the first thing in its block. No eyebrow, category label, small uppercase heading or back link sits above it. Nothing here is set in uppercase. A line that says more about a heading goes under it, as the index's name line does.

rules.name: The One Strip Rule
rules.body: The index is a single strip: no cards, no bands, no second column of content. Anything new on it is a row, name left and value right, or a group of rows under a dashed rule. The closing row stays last, and the pink pill stays under it.

rules.name: The Fixed First Row Rule
rules.body: The strip's first row keeps its height whatever fills it, so what the browser remembers can arrive late without moving anything under a finger.

rules.name: The Slab Rule, for tools
rules.body: A tool page opens with a title band and never closes with one: on a phone, the tool comes before the frame.

rules.name: The First Screen Rule
rules.body: On a phone, the first field of a tool is visible without scrolling. If a new element would push it down, it belongs lower on the page.

rules.name: The Answer In Reach Rule
rules.body: Wherever a tool is being filled in, its answer is one glance or one tap away: the running total below 1024 px, the split's own column above. Someone opening a shared result lands on it, not on the form that made it.

rules.name: The Only Floating Things Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons, chips, bands, the strip and the running total never get a drop shadow. A control or a strip row responds by filling with the next tonal step, and its arrow moves 4 px on.

rules.name: The Value Right Rule
rules.body: On the strip, what something gives you is set right, where the eye looks for the amount; what it is stays left. Never swap them, and never center a row.

rules.name: The Whole Edge Rule
rules.body: A note is marked by its whole edge, never by a thick bar down one side.

dos: Do take tokens, radii, button shapes, the arrow and type roles from itrium.id's DESIGN.md before inventing anything. A difference between the two sites needs a reason a tool has and a page doesn't.
Do keep a tool's first field on the first phone screen.
Do give every field, button and chip a `--control-border` edge and a touch target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens.

Do show every state in two ways: a check mark with the pink fill, words with the pink edge, and the reason a button can't be pressed yet, said under it when someone presses or reaches it (not at rest, and not read out again after every add).
Do design and check every new pairing in light and dark, on every surface it sits on.
Do use the drawn arrow wherever a link points onward.

Do keep motion in CSS, gated on `motion-safe` or `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`: page cross-fades, the 4 px arrow nudge, and the loading spinner. Nothing in a tool rises or reveals as it scrolls.
Do add to the index as a row of the strip: a name on the left, its value set right in tabular figures, inside a group under a dashed rule.
Do use Tailwind classes with the theme tokens and the shared classes in `src/lib/styles.ts`, never raw hex values in markup.
donts: Don't use pink as decoration, or put two pink buttons in one view.
Don't put a small uppercase heading, eyebrow, kicker or back link above a heading.
Don't type arrows or chevrons as characters.
Don't give cards, buttons, chips, bands or the running total a drop shadow.
Don't use `#000000` or pure white text on pink. Graphite is `#2b2b2b`.
Don't put pastel pink text or lines on a light background.
Don't use a native `<select>`, inline styles, `data:` URLs, or anything from another domain.
Don't add gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers, or a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen.
Don't set field text below 16px on touch screens.
Don't put cards, bands or a hero on the index, or dress the strip as a receipt: no torn edges, prices, "TOTAL", shop header or thank-you line.
